root.name: Scotch Game: Blumenfeld Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5 5. Be3 Qf6 6. Nb5

overview: After 4...Bc5 5.Be3 Qf6 White jumps 6.Nb5, threatening Nxc7+ and Bxc5, and the game turns on tactics: Black can take the bishop pair on e3 or defend c7 with ...Kd8-style resources. Strong players rarely meet it, and reliable evidence on the best defence is thin.

white_ideas.idea: Threaten Nxc7+ with the knight on b5
Trade or win time against the c5 bishop with Be3
Open lines for the pieces quickly with c3 or Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Defend c7 and develop with ...Kd8 or ...Bb6 lines
Use the f6 queen against f2 and b2

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after the d-pawn exchange with the king stuck in the centre for one side

character.notes: Forcing tactical skirmish around c7, f2 and the king in the centre.

gambit.notes: No material is given on purpose in the main line.

soundness.notes: Believed dubious for White but unsure; I do not recognise the details of the best defence.

structure.notes: Open centre, pieces fighting for open lines immediately.

approach.notes: A rare Scotch sideline that strong players hardly play.

level.notes: Tactics must be known precisely; not for beginners.

character.reason: Forcing tactics around c7 and f2 from move six.
